links.comparator_used: O-RAG: same knowledge base and GPT-4o model without patient-specific clinical parameters (3-arm pilot RCT, also standard care)
links.outcome: Change in medication and dietary information needs (5-point Likert) from baseline to 4 weeks
links.effect: C-RAG vs O-RAG: lower needs in both domains (observed mean 2.93, SD 1.21 vs mean 3.86, SD 0.95; Cohen d=-0.86, 95% CI -1.63 to -0.08; P=.02 for both). C-RAG vs standard care: medium-to-large but nonsignificant effects (medication d=-0.64, 95% CI -1.39 to 0.12; dietary d=-0.54, 95% CI -1.30 to 0.21). Secondary outcomes did not differ between groups.
links.quote: In this pilot trial, personalized RAG showed lower information needs than general RAG, with a large effect size

links.comparator_used: O-RAG: same knowledge base without personalization, with no added patient clinical parameters
links.outcome: Change in medication and dietary information needs from baseline to 4 weeks
links.effect: C-RAG lower than O-RAG (mean 2.93, SD 1.21 vs 3.86, SD 0.95; Cohen d=-0.86, 95% CI -1.63 to -0.08; P=.02). ANCOVA group differences for medication (F2,38=4.574, P=.02) and dietary (F2,38=4.232, P=.02) needs.
links.quote: In this pilot trial, personalized RAG showed lower information needs than general RAG, with a large effect size

design_hint: Personalized retrieval grounding with patient-specific clinical parameters
